examples.en: He is all smooth talk and his actions don't follow.
His face was shiny and greasy because of the oil.
I wore shoes with a glossy shine.
He is a person who is only shiny on the surface.

examples.ko: 번지르르 말은 잘하는데 믿음이 안 가요.
examples.en: He talks smoothly, but I don't trust him.

examples.ko: 손에 로션을 발랐더니 번지르르 윤이 났어요.
examples.en: After I put lotion on my hands, they became glossy.

explain: 반들반들 윤이 나는 모습을 말하지만, 실제로는 '겉만 번지르르하다', '말만 번지르르하다'처럼 겉이나 말만 그럴듯하고 속은 부족하다는 부정적인 뉘앙스로 많이 써요. 보통 '번지르르하다/번지르르한' 형태로 써요.

phrases.example: 이 가게는 겉만 번지르르하고 음식 맛은 별로예요.
phrases.en: This restaurant only looks good on the outside, and the food is not great.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이나 말은 그럴듯한데 알맹이는 부족할 때 비판하는 말투로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used critically when the appearance or words sound impressive but the substance is lacking.

explain_en: It describes a smooth, shiny look, but in practice it is often used negatively, as in '겉만 번지르르하다' or '말만 번지르르하다', meaning it only looks or sounds good on the outside. It is usually used in the forms '번지르르하다' or '번지르르한'.

en: to be bustling; to be fussy

examples.en: The market is bustling from morning with merchants.
Guests came, so the kitchen was in a flurry for a while.
The meeting began in a hectic atmosphere.
The station will be bustling because the holiday is near.

examples.ko: 부산하게 짐을 싸는 모습이 눈에 띄었어요.
examples.en: The hurried way they packed stood out.

examples.ko: 사무실이 부산하지 않아서 일이 잘 돼요.
examples.en: The office isn't hectic, so work goes well.

explain: 도시 이름 '부산'과 소리가 같지만 다른 말이에요. '바쁘다'는 할 일이 많은 것이고, '부산하다'는 움직이는 모습이 어수선하고 서두르는 것이에요. '부산스럽다'와 비슷하게 써요.

phrases.example: 저녁이 되면 부산한 거리에 사람이 많아져요.
phrases.en: In the evening the bustling street gets crowded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 꾸미는 활용형이에요. 사람들이 바쁘게 오가는 장소에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, which fits places where people come and go busily.

phrases.en: On holiday mornings the family moves around busily.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게' 형태로 동사를 꾸밀 수 있어요. 서두르고 어수선한 움직임을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-게' form modifies a verb, describing hurried and restless movement.

phrases.en: The kids are so restless that I can't think straight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 사람이나 아이의 모습에 조금 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning; used a little more often for people or children.

explain_en: It sounds like the city name '부산' but is a different word. '바쁘다' means having a lot to do, while '부산하다' describes the hurried, disorderly look of people moving around. It is used much like '부산스럽다'.

dis.h: busy and hectic with movement and noise

p.n: 부산스럽다 leans toward fussy, restless behavior.

en: to be savage; to be bloody

examples.en: It's exam season, so the atmosphere in the library is tense and grim.

examples.ko: 두 사람 사이가 살벌해서 말을 못 걸었어요.
examples.en: The mood between the two was so hostile that I couldn't talk to them.
Prices have risen brutally these days.
He stared at me with a fierce look, and I was scared.
The mood in the meeting was really harsh.
I heard the rent in this neighborhood is brutal.

explain: 분위기, 눈빛, 말투가 차갑고 적대적이라 긴장될 때 써요. '무섭다'와 달리 서로 맞서는 긴장감이 있고, 말할 때는 '살벌하게 비싸다'처럼 강조하는 말로도 써요.

phrases.example: 회의실이 살벌한 분위기여서 아무도 말을 못 했어요.
phrases.en: The meeting room had such a tense atmosphere that nobody could speak.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차갑고 긴장돼서 숨쉬기 어려운 분위기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a cold, tense atmosphere that is hard to breathe in.

phrases.example: 그 사람이 살벌한 눈빛으로 저를 쳐다봤어요.
phrases.en: That person stared at me with a menacing look.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화가 나서 적대적으로 보는 눈을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes eyes that look angry and hostile.

phrases.en: House prices in this neighborhood are brutally expensive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 '아주 심하게'라는 뜻으로 강조하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, an intensifier meaning 'extremely'.

explain_en: It describes an atmosphere, look or tone that is cold and hostile, creating tension. Unlike '무섭다', it carries a sense of confrontation, and in speech it can also be an intensifier, as in '살벌하게 비싸다'.

en: to be infallible; to be punctual

examples.ko: 월급날이면 어김없이 은행 앱에서 알림이 와요.
examples.en: On payday, a notification always arrives from my banking app.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 시간 약속이 어김없는 사람이에요.
examples.en: He is someone who never fails to keep a time appointment.
His calculations are always spot on.
When spring comes, the cherry blossoms bloom without fail.
It's an undeniable fact, so you can trust it.
I hate Mondays that come around without fail.

explain: 대부분 '어김없이'로 써요. '꼭', '틀림없이'와 비슷한데, '때가 되면 늘 그대로 반복된다'는 느낌이 강해요. 봄이 오는 것이나 월급날처럼 정해진 일에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: When autumn came, the leaves changed color without fail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어의 부사형이고 실제로 가장 많이 써요. 때가 되면 늘 그대로 일어난다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the adverb form and by far the most common one. It gives the feeling that something happens just as expected when the time comes.

phrases.en: He keeps his promises without fail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속이나 규칙을 한 번도 빼먹지 않고 지킨다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means keeping a promise or rule every time without missing once.

phrases.en: It will surely rain tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어김없이'와 비슷하지만, 반복되는 느낌보다 확실하다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 어김없이, but it stresses certainty more than repetition.

explain_en: It is mostly used as '어김없이'. It resembles '꼭' and '틀림없이', but carries a stronger sense that something repeats as expected whenever its time comes. It fits fixed events, like the arrival of spring or payday.

examples.ko: 다른 사람과 비교하면 내가 열등하다고 느껴질 때가 있어요.
examples.en: When I compare myself with others, sometimes I feel inferior.

examples.ko: 어떤 문화가 우월하거나 열등한 것은 아니에요.
examples.en: No culture is superior or inferior.

examples.ko: 남보다 열등해 보일까 봐 발표하기가 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I'm worried about presenting because I might look inferior to others.

examples.ko: 성적만으로 사람을 열등하게 보면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't look down on a person as inferior based only on grades.

examples.ko: 제 실력이 다른 선수보다 열등해서 속상했어요.
examples.en: I was upset because my skill was inferior to the other player's.

examples.ko: 자신이 열등하지 않다는 걸 증명하고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I wanted to prove that I'm not inferior.

explain: '못하다'보다 무겁고 강한 말이라서 사람에게 쓰면 기분 나쁘게 들릴 수 있어요. 반대말은 '우월하다'이고, 일상에서는 '열등감'이라는 말을 더 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 친구와 비교하면 열등감이 들 때가 있어요.
phrases.en: Sometimes I feel inferior when I compare myself with my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '열등하다'보다 이 말을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life this is used more often than 열등하다 itself.

phrases.example: 다른 사람과 비교하면 제 실력이 열등해 보여요.
phrases.en: Compared with other people, my skills look inferior.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보이다'를 붙이면 겉으로 그렇게 보인다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 보이다 gives the sense that it merely looks that way.

phrases.example: 우리 팀은 다른 팀보다 열등하지 않아요.
phrases.en: Our team is not inferior to the other teams.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 써서 '못하지 않다'는 뜻을 강하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form firmly says 'not any worse'.

explain_en: It is heavier and stronger than '못하다' (to be poor at), so it can sound hurtful when applied to a person. The opposite is '우월하다' (superior), and in daily life people use '열등감' (inferiority complex) more often.

examples.en: I heard that proactivity is important in interviews.
The teacher praised the students' proactivity.

examples.ko: 팀에서 적극성만 있다고 일이 잘되는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Having proactivity alone doesn't make work go well in a team.
Proactivity is needed, but consideration matters too.
Everyone was surprised by his drive.

examples.ko: 동생은 적극성이 부족해서 손을 잘 안 들어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling lacks initiative and rarely raises a hand.

explain: '적극성이 있다/없다/부족하다'처럼 말하고, 반대말은 '소극성'이에요. 사람을 직접 설명할 때는 '적극적이다'가 더 자주 쓰여요. 면접, 수업, 회사 이야기에서 칭찬이나 아쉬운 점을 말할 때 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: The new employee is proactive about work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성격이나 태도를 직접 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a person's character or attitude directly.

phrases.en: That student shows enthusiasm in class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행동으로 드러난 태도를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the attitude shows in actions.

phrases.example: 제가 발표할 때 적극성이 부족하다는 말을 들었어요.
phrases.en: I was told that I lack enthusiasm when I present.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아쉬운 점을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to point out a shortcoming.

explain_en: You say '적극성이 있다/없다/부족하다', and the opposite is '소극성'. To describe a person directly, '적극적이다' is used more often. It comes up in interviews, classes and the workplace when praising someone or noting a shortcoming.

en: to be enormous; to be great

examples.ko: 스승의 가르침은 제 인생에 지대한 영향을 줬어요.
examples.en: My teacher's lessons had an immense influence on my life.

examples.ko: 그 소식에 대한 사람들의 관심이 지대했어요.
examples.en: People's interest in that news was huge.

examples.ko: 이 사고가 지역 경제에 끼칠 피해가 지대할 거예요.
examples.en: The damage this accident will do to the local economy will be great.
Parents play a hugely important role in a child's growth.
His contribution is immense, and everyone acknowledges it.

examples.ko: 그 발명이 사회에 미친 영향이 얼마나 지대했는지 몰라요.
examples.en: You can't imagine how great the invention's impact on society was.

explain: '지대하다'는 영향·관심·공처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것이 아주 클 때만 써요. 물건이나 건물의 크기에는 '크다'를 써요. 뉴스나 글에서 '지대한 영향', '지대한 관심'으로 굳어서 나오고, 말할 때는 '아주 크다', '엄청나다'가 더 많이 들려요.

phrases.example: 부모의 말은 아이에게 지대한 영향을 줘요.
phrases.en: Parents' words have a great influence on a child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이고 주로 글에서 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, mostly seen in writing.

phrases.example: 많은 사람이 그 일에 지대한 관심을 보여요.
phrases.en: Many people show great interest in that matter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 관심이 아주 클 때 '지대한 관심'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Say 지대한 관심 when interest is very great.

phrases.example: 그 일이 저에게 미친 영향은 아주 커요.
phrases.en: The effect that had on me is very big.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '아주 크다'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: 아주 크다 sounds more natural in speech.

explain_en: 지대하다 is used only for things you can't see, such as influence, interest, or contribution. For physical size, use 크다. It appears mostly as set phrases like 지대한 영향 and 지대한 관심 in news and writing; in speech, people say 아주 크다 or 엄청나다.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 품성이 따뜻해서 모두가 좋아해요.
examples.en: He has a warm character, so everyone likes him.

examples.ko: 아이의 품성은 가정 교육에서 많이 길러져요.
examples.en: A child's character is largely shaped by upbringing at home.

examples.ko: 좋은 품성을 가진 사람과 일하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to work with people of good character.
I heard interviewers look closely at an applicant's character too.
Thanks to his excellent character, he even received an award.
There is nothing to criticize about his character.

explain: '성격'은 밝다, 급하다처럼 타고난 기질까지 두루 말하지만, '품성'은 사람 됨됨이, 곧 인품과 도덕적인 면을 말할 때 써요. 그래서 '품성이 좋다, 바르다'처럼 칭찬하는 문장에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 좋은 품성을 가진 사람이 되고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to be a person of good character.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람직한 사람 됨됨이를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for desirable personal character.

phrases.en: That student was praised for having upright character.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예의 바르고 도덕적인 사람을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Praises someone who is polite and moral.

phrases.example: 책을 읽으면 품성을 기를 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Reading can help you build character.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교육이나 경험으로 길러 간다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests developing character through education or experience.

explain_en: '성격' covers temperament in general, such as cheerful or hasty, but '품성' is about a person's moral character and quality. That is why it often appears in praise like '품성이 좋다' or '품성이 바르다'.

en: to be boundless; to be endless; to be limitless

examples.en: The love my parents gave me is truly boundless.
I don't know how to repay my endless gratitude.
I was endlessly happy when I heard I passed.
She comforted the child with an infinitely gentle voice.

examples.ko: 그 말을 들으니 제 자신이 한없이 작아졌어요.
examples.en: Hearing those words, I felt infinitely small.

examples.ko: 한없던 슬픔도 시간이 지나니 조금씩 줄었어요.
examples.en: Even my endless sadness slowly lessened as time passed.

explain: '끝없다'는 길, 바다처럼 눈에 보이는 것에도 많이 쓰고, '한없다'는 사랑, 기쁨, 슬픔 같은 마음에 자주 써요. 대부분 '한없이' 꼴로 나오고, '한없는 사랑'처럼 꾸밀 때는 '한없는'을 써요.

phrases.en: I was endlessly happy to hear I passed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '한없이'는 형용사 앞에 붙어 마음이 끝이 없이 크다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 한없이 before an adjective adds a sense of boundless feeling.

phrases.en: I'm endlessly grateful for your help.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고마움이 매우 크다는 걸 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to express very deep gratitude.

phrases.en: The endlessly stretching sea was beautiful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 보이는 길이나 바다에도 쓸 수 있어서 '한없다'보다 넓게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also be used for visible things like roads or the sea, so it is broader than 한없다.

explain_en: '끝없다' is often used for visible things like roads or the sea, while '한없다' is often used for feelings such as love, joy and sadness. It mostly appears as '한없이', and '한없는' is used to modify a noun, as in '한없는 사랑' (boundless love).

en: to be bright; to be innocent; to be clear

examples.en: The child's smile is truly bright and innocent.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 늘 해맑은 얼굴로 인사해요.
examples.en: That child always greets people with a bright, innocent face.

examples.ko: 해맑게 웃는 모습을 보면 기분이 좋아져요.
examples.en: Seeing her laugh so brightly makes me feel good.
Puppies are so carefree that just seeing them makes me happy.

examples.ko: 어른이 되어도 해맑은 마음을 잃고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: Even as an adult, I don't want to lose my innocent heart.

examples.ko: 그는 해맑았던 어린 시절을 가끔 떠올려요.
examples.en: He sometimes remembers his innocent childhood.

explain: '해맑다'는 얼굴이나 웃음이 맑고 순수해서 걱정이 없어 보일 때 써요. 아이나 강아지처럼 순수한 대상에 주로 쓰고, 어른에게 쓰면 철이 없다는 뜻으로 들릴 때도 있어요. '해맑게 웃다'로 가장 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The baby looked at me and smiled brightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해맑다'를 부사형으로 써서 웃는 모습을 꾸며요. 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form describes how someone smiles. It is the most common collocation.

phrases.example: 그 아이의 해맑은 미소에 기분이 좋아졌어요.
phrases.en: The child's pure smile made me feel good.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해맑다'를 명사 앞에 붙인 활용형이에요. 순수하고 밝은 웃음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form before a noun, meaning a pure, bright smile.

phrases.example: 강아지가 마당에서 뛰어놀 때 해맑아 보여요.
phrases.en: The puppy looks so carefree when it plays in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보이다'로 겉모습이 그렇게 느껴질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -아/어 보이다 it describes how something appears.

explain_en: '해맑다' describes a face or smile that is clear and pure, looking free of worries. It is used mostly for children and puppies, and for an adult it can sometimes sound like naive. The usual phrase is '해맑게 웃다'.

en: to be countless; to be plenty; to be numerous

examples.en: Things like that are everywhere around us.
Plenty of people were late because of the traffic.

examples.ko: 요즘 이런 사기 전화는 허다하다고 해요.
examples.en: They say scam calls like this are everywhere these days.

examples.ko: 이 동네에는 빈 가게가 허다해서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: There are plenty of empty shops in this neighborhood, which worries me.

examples.ko: 시험에 떨어지는 경우도 허다하니까 너무 걱정하지 마세요.
examples.en: Failing an exam happens all the time, so don't worry too much.

examples.ko: 주말에는 줄을 서는 가게가 허다할 거예요.
examples.en: On weekends, there will be plenty of shops with lines.

explain: '흔하다'와 비슷하지만 '허다하다'는 글이나 뉴스, 어른의 말투에 어울리는 딱딱한 말이에요. 주로 '~는 경우가 허다하다', '~는 사람이 허다하다'처럼 수가 아주 많다고 말할 때 써요. 가벼운 대화에서는 '많아요', '흔해요'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: There are plenty of cases of being late for appointments.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그런 경우가 아주 많다고 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form for saying such cases are very numerous.

phrases.en: There are plenty of people who sleep in on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그런 사람이 아주 많다고 말할 때 써요. '경우' 대신 '사람'이나 '일'을 넣어 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say there are very many such people. You can put 'person' or 'thing' in place of 'case'.

phrases.en: Nowadays that kind of thing is common.
phrases.nuance_ko: '허다하다'보다 부드럽고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than 'heodahada' and more common in daily conversation.

explain_en: It is similar to '흔하다', but '허다하다' is stiffer and fits writing, news and adult speech. It is mostly used in patterns like '~는 경우가 허다하다' or '~는 사람이 허다하다' to say there are very many. In casual talk, '많아요' or '흔해요' sounds more natural.
